subject: Critical Thinking
title: Peter Singer and Effective Altruism: Ethics by the Numbers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Peter Singer and Effective Altruism: Ethics by the Numbers usable.

hook.text: A child is drowning in a pond. You'd ruin your $200 shoes to save them.

buildup.text: Peter Singer's argument: physical distance doesn't change moral obligation.

discovery.text: Effective altruism: use evidence & reason to determine the most effective ways to help others.

twist.text: Critics say effective altruism can flatten ethics into spreadsheets and miss dignity, duty, and loyalty.

climax.text: Singer's challenge remains powerful: we routinely spend on luxuries while others die from preventable causes.

quiz.question: What is Peter Singer's core argument about distance and moral obligation?
options: We should only help people we can see
Physical distance doesn't reduce our moral obligation to prevent suffering
Charity should be limited to our community

details.summary: Peter Singer's effective altruism applies utilitarian reasoning to charitable giving, arguing we should donate where each dollar saves the most lives. It treats philanthropy as an optimization problem with measurable outcomes.
details.whyItMatters: Effective altruism has redirected billions in donations toward evidence-based interventions and reshaped how people think about charity.
takeaways: Charity should be guided by evidence of impact, not emotion
Some causes save far more lives per dollar than others
Singer argues affluent people have strong obligations to give

faq.question: What makes effective altruism different from traditional charity?
faq.answer: It prioritizes measurable impact per dollar over emotional appeal. Instead of giving to whichever cause moves you, you give where evidence shows the greatest benefit.

faq.question: What are common critiques of the effective altruism movement?
faq.answer: Critics argue it overemphasizes quantifiable outcomes, neglects systemic change, and can be elitist by assuming Western donors know best how to help others.
